cap: Acyclovir is inactive until the virus switches it on. Viral thymidine kinase adds the first phosphate, host kinases finish the triphosphate, and viral DNA polymerase inserts it and stalls. Uninfected cells lack the viral kinase, which gives the drug its selectivity. A virus that loses the kinase escapes, which is why foscarnet, needing no activation, treats resistant herpes.
teach: Valacyclovir and famciclovir follow the same path after the body converts them to acyclovir and penciclovir, so a thymidine kinase mutant is resistant to all three. Because acyclovir acts only on replicating virus, it shortens outbreaks and suppresses shedding but cannot touch the silent viral genome in the sacral ganglia, so herpes returns when the drug stops.
